# Edwin Jesu Dass — edwinjd.com

> Portfolio and writing hub of Edwin Jesu Dass, a Malaysia-based construction and digital transformation practitioner, writer, and speaker.

## Overview

This site is the personal portfolio and publishing platform of Edwin Jesu Dass. It contains:

- A professional portfolio covering construction, digital transformation, AI in construction management, and ESG leadership
- Auto-updating Medium article feeds
- The Observatory — a collection of social media sentiment analyses mapping discourse, sarcasm, and bilingual code-switching in Malaysian online comment sections

## Key Pages

- [Home / Portfolio](https://edwinjd.com/) — About, selected work, latest Medium articles, contact
- [The Observatory](https://edwinjd.com/analyses.html) — Gallery of social media sentiment analyses
- [Rohingya Sentiment Analysis](https://edwinjd.com/rohingya-sentiment.html) — AI-powered classification of 981 Facebook comments with contextual understanding of English, Malay, and code-switched language
- [Johor PRN 2022 vs GE15](https://edwinjd.com/johor-elections.html) — Seat-by-seat electoral analysis comparing the Johor state election and federal election eight months apart
- [Malaysia Job Loss 2026](https://edwinjd.com/malaysia-job-loss-2026.html) — Dashboard, infographic, and policy brief on Malaysia's 2026 retrenchment surge and labour-market safety-net gaps
- [FIFA World Cup Ticket Prices](https://edwinjd.com/wc-ticket-prices.html) — Dashboard, infographic, and analysis brief on World Cup ticket inflation, affordability gaps, and the 2026 dynamic-pricing shock
- [MOH Hospital Fee Reform Revenue Forecast](https://edwinjd.com/moh-fee-forecast.html) — Hypothetical healthcare policy model forecasting outpatient fee reform, restricted-goods surcharge mechanics, and frontliner welfare funding in Malaysia
- [Swarm Governance Framework](https://edwinjd.com/swarm-governance.html) — DBA research proposal on AI-enabled swarm governance via Design Science Research

## Projects

### The Observatory (Social Media Sentiment Analysis)
A personal research project analysing Facebook comment sentiment on viral Malaysian news articles. Uses contextual rule-based classification trained on bilingual (English + Bahasa Malaysia) linguistic patterns, addressing limitations of standard English sentiment models (VADER) that misclassify Malay dismissals and sarcastic positivity as neutral or positive.

## Tech Stack

- Static HTML/CSS/JS
- No build step required
- Chart.js for data visualisations
- GitHub Pages hosting
- Auto-updating Medium RSS feed via JavaScript
